steps.observation: Work on this for 60 seconds; do not stop early. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
A Transformer is a sequence-processing architecture built almost entirely around “self-attention” rather than recurrence or convolutions.  Conceptually it works like this:

1. Input Representation  
   • You start by turning each input token (word, subword, etc.) into a fixed-size vector via an embedding lookup.  
   • Because attention treats all positions symmetrically, you add a “positional encoding” (sine/cosine or learned) so the model still knows the order of tokens.

2. Self-Attention Mechanism  
   • For each position you compute three vectors—Query (Q), Key (K) and Value (V)—by multiplying the embedding by three learned matrices.  
   • To figure out how much position i should “attend” to position j, you take the dot-product of Qi with Kj, scale it, and run it through softmax. That gives you attention weights.  
   • You multiply those weights against the V vectors and sum them up. The result is a new representation for position i that blends information from everywhere in the sequence.

3. Multi-Head Attention  
   • Instead of doing one single attention pass, you split Q, K, V into several “heads” (sub-vectors), do attention in parallel, then concatenate.  
   • Different heads can focus on different kinds of relationships (e.g. syntax vs. long-range context).

4. Position-Wise Feed-Forward & Residuals  
   • After attention, each position’s vector goes through the same small feed-forward network (two linear layers with a nonlinearity in between).  
   • Around both the multi-head attention and the feed-forward sublayers you add residual connections (“add the input back in”) and then layer-normalize. This stabilizes training and helps gradient flow.

5. Stacking Layers  
   • You repeat the block (multi-head attention → add & norm → feed-forward → add & norm) N times to get a deep encoder.  
   • In a full encoder–decoder Transformer (e.g. for translation), the decoder has an extra “encoder–decoder attention” layer that lets each decoder position attend to all encoder outputs, plus masking in its self-attention so it can’t peek at future tokens.

6. Output and Generation  
   • In the decoder’s final layer you project each position’s vector into a distribution over your vocabulary (via a linear layer + softmax).  
   • At inference time you generate tokens one by one (auto-regressively), feeding each newly generated token back in to predict the next.

Key Intuition  
– Self-attention lets every token repeatedly ask “which other tokens should I look at most?” and update its own representation accordingly.  
– Multi-head attention lets the model capture several different “views” of context in parallel.  
– The whole thing stacks so you can build up from local, shallow interactions in early layers to very abstract, global features in deeper layers.

That’s the crux of how Transformers replace recurrence with parallelizable attention to achieve both speed and state-of-the-art performance on language, vision, and more.
